Delaware Property Tax Guide: Appeals, Exemptions and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Delaware
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs

Selling a Delaware House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Delaware statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Delaware property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • New Castle County: written notice of assessment appeal must be filed with the Board of Assessment Review before March 15; Board gives at least 10 days' notice of hearing; failure to appear is abandonment. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I (Board of Assessment Review); source)
  • Kent and Sussex Boards of Assessment Review hear appeals from March 1 to May 31 each year (or until all appeals are heard in a reassessment year). (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • If an appeal reduces assessed value and the owner overpaid by $50 or more, the owner is entitled to a refund; under $50 the county may refund or credit it. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • The board must notify the appellant of its decision in writing by registered mail within 30 days of the decision. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • An aggrieved appellant may appeal to Superior Court within 30 days (postmark) after receiving notice of the decision; the board's decision is prima facie correct and the appellant must show it acted contrary to law, fraudulently, arbitrarily or capriciously. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • Delinquent-tax sales are advertised by handbills in at least 10 public places (one on the land, one at the courthouse) and a newspaper notice; sales occur at the courthouse door. (9 Del. C. ch. 87, subch. IV; source)
  • The court will not approve a sale if the owner is ready at court to pay taxes, penalty and costs. (9 Del. C. ch. 87, subch. IV; source)
Selling in Delaware?

Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Details we could not confirm on an official page are not stated.

How to sell a Delaware house when this applies to you

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Delaware.

What a cash sale of a Delaware house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Delaware.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Delaware disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Delaware

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Delaware change, so confirm details with the official office or a Delaware attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Delaware

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

The closing agent pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.

This guide covers Delaware foreclosure sales according to official sources. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • A purchaser at a sheriff's sale under a mortgage scire facias holds the property free of the mortgagor's equity of redemption and incumbrances. (10 Del. C. § 5066; source)
  • No judgment may be entered, and no covered owner-occupied 1-4 family residence sold at sheriff's sale, unless the plaintiff has filed the loss-mitigation affidavit. (10 Del. C. § 5062A(b); source)
  • Seller disclosure law does not apply to transfers by sheriff's sale for default on a mortgage, judgment, tax or other lien. (6 Del. C. § 2577(4); source)
  • Delinquent-tax sales are advertised by handbills in at least 10 public places in the county and a newspaper notice, with sales at the courthouse door. (9 Del. C. ch. 87, subch. IV; source)
  • Foreclosure is judicial: the mortgagee sues out a writ of scire facias sur mortgage in the Superior Court of the county where the property lies. (10 Del. C. § 5061(a); source)
  • For owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences, a foreclosure action may not be filed until 45 days after a notice of intent to foreclose is sent by certified and first-class mail. (10 Del. C. § 5062B(a); source)
  • Plaintiff must file a loss-mitigation affidavit before judgment or sheriff's sale on owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences. (10 Del. C. § 5062A; source)
  • An Automatic Residential Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program applies to owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences; a mediation notice accompanies the complaint. (10 Del. C. § 5062C; source)
  • A buyer at the foreclosure sale holds the property discharged from all equity of redemption and incumbrances made by the mortgagor. (10 Del. C. § 5066; source)
